items.PAYLOAD: Theory document defines adaptive epistemic systems around empirical modification of reasoning mechanisms while maintaining reality-to-future-behavior coupling.

Theory claims intelligence depends on persistent mechanism improvement, distinguishes fixed-structure optimization, treats contradiction as selection pressure, frames authority dynamics as internal selection, distinguishes learning from mechanism-changing adaptive intelligence, and defines the endpoint as reality-driven mechanism change under stability.
Formal theory gives Reality->Feedback->Internal Change->Future Behavior, contradiction-to-structural-improvement sequence, parameter/policy/mechanism/representation hierarchy, and dOmega/dt<=Theta C.
Conceptual architecture comprises mechanisms, authority weights, residual detection, attribution, correction, and representation expansion.
Causal authority is the ability of a mechanism to retain or lose power over future reasoning while remaining present.

Predicts authority-dynamic systems will outperform output/memory/policy-only adaptation on long horizons and show lower recurrence, faster shift recovery, improved viability, and better representation change.
Causal-authority measurement, expansion stopping criteria, stability-bound validation, and empirical baseline comparison remain unresolved.
Related-work surface situates the theory across machine learning, cognitive science, evolution, control, and AI safety around evidence-driven mechanism-authority changes.

Authored comparisons distinguish the proposed authority layer from RL, Bayesian inference, predictive processing, continual learning, evolutionary computation, mechanistic interpretability, memory systems, recursive AI, and alignment research.

Proposes regulation of causal authority as an additional layer and claims long-horizon adaptation requires experience to reshape internal learning/reasoning structures while acknowledging neighboring fields contain adaptive components.
Comparison table summarizes neighboring fields by their source-described primary focus.
Systematic comparative evidence, terminology-equivalence analysis, mapping from interpretability to authority control, and sufficiency for alignment remain unresolved.
Document defines unresolved theoretical and experimental problems for the research program.

Open problems cover update-law selection, causal attribution, mechanism granularity, authority-distribution structure, restoration stability, expansion thresholds, alternative-mechanism comparison, scaling, alignment sufficiency, diagnostic environments, emergent reasoning, consciousness/agency, and empirical validation.
Candidate relationship Intelligence proportional to C_improve is explicitly posed within an open question about whether adaptive improvement is fundamental or one intelligence dimension.
Framework is framed as a hypothesis about a necessary property of highly adaptive systems, while whether authority dynamics is an engineering pattern or deeper principle remains open.
Fourteen explicit unresolved ceilings preserve the absence of empirical selection/measurement/validation across every named open problem.
